title: feat(rate-limit): add public Valkey facade
reason: Package was a pure re-export of Valkyries with no platform-owned behavior; Filaments already depended on Valkyries directly, so it only added release/dependency maintenance.

expected.claim: This entire package is a nine-line re-export (with a few renames) of valkyries; it adds a new published boundary, release entry and dependency-policy surface without any behavior of its own. Consumers can depend on valkyries directly, so this facade should not be extracted.

title: feat(votes): add generic vote engine
reason: Over-extracted application-shaped HTTP vote mutation lifecycle before a second independent consumer; first consumer stayed line-neutral and still needed a large adapter.

expected.claim: createVoteHandler bakes an application-shaped request lifecycle (auth, route rate limits, access hooks, 404/422/429 policy, noop handling) behind many injected hooks and six generic parameters. With only one consumer this boundary is speculative and the consumer will still need a large adapter, so it should stay in the product until a second consumer shows the real shared surface.

title: feat(storage): normalize messaging and distribution relations
reason: Chat message envelope {role, content, error} holds no entity ids; under the settled storage rule (only entity ids / UUID arrays of entity ids become FKs or child rows, structured documents stay JSON) it should have stayed jsonb. Only the chat typing was reverted.

expected.claim: The chat envelope (role, text, error) contains no entity references, so splitting it into chat_role/chat_text/chat_error columns plus a new enum and cross-column CHECKs does not follow the repo storage rule that only entity ids become relations while structured documents stay JSON. This adds schema and service churn without enforcing any relation.

title: feat(utils): add HTTP runtime helpers
feat(embeds): split local and remote resolution
feat: extract generic Filaments utilities
fix(workspace-gates): ban dependency version assertions in tests
feat(storage): normalize ingestion and reconciliation facts
reason: Ingestion payloads (query strings, crawl links, embed documents, SES recipients, boilerplate results, admin import input) were split into child tables/columns although they are documents, not joinable entity references; restored to jsonb under the storage rule.

expected.claim: boilerplate_removal_results turns an opaque list of selector/HTML strings into an ordered child table. Those values are extractor payload, not references to other entities, so the repo storage rule says they stay JSON rather than becoming rows with ordinal bookkeeping. The same applies to the other ingestion documents (crawl links, embed metadata, SES recipients) converted in this PR.

This normalization adds many tables, ordinals, partition-drop special cases and rewritten writers/readers (about 80 files) for data that is only ever read back whole. The relational model buys no integrity or query benefit here, so the approach is over-engineered for payloads.

title: feat(communities): normalize application options and answers
reason: Option labels and typed answers were exploded into option, answer and selection tables with triggers; only question-id references should be relational, so options went back to a JSON label array and answers to one row per question with a JSON value.

expected.claim: community_application_question_options stores an ordered list of display labels as rows with order-cap and uniqueness constraints. Labels are a structured document, not entity references, so under the storage rule the option list should remain a JSON array on the question.

The answer-selection table plus assertion functions and triggers re-implement what a typed value with a CHECK could enforce. Three tables and cross-table triggers for one answer value is heavier than needed; only the question reference needs a foreign key.

title: feat(gha-pr-checkpoint): add resume selection and update helpers
reason: Resume/update helpers ignored caller-supplied checkpoint marker options and always used the default marker, so any consumer with a custom marker could never resume or update.

expected.claim: selectResumeCheckpoint calls sortedCheckpointCandidates without forwarding codec options, so a caller using its own checkpoint marker will never match. Accept and thread the codec options through, and add a test with a non-default marker.

updateExactCheckpoint parses the existing comment with parseCheckpoint using default options, so custom-marker comments are rejected as not matching the run binding. Thread the same codec options here; the tests only use the library default marker, which hides this.

title: feat(ci): restore the Claude code-review reusable workflow
reason: Cleanup steps in the composite deleted the checked-out action directory that runner post-job hooks still need, failing the job after a successful review.

expected.claim: This step removes the workspace .vouchington-tooling directory, which is the composite action own checkout. The runner still has post-job hooks (from the nested checkout step) that need to resolve the action metadata there, so deleting it can fail the job even when the review succeeded. Leave the checkout in place for runner teardown.
The final cleanup also deletes the action checkout path, with the same post-hook resolution hazard; keep it until teardown.

title: Automation scheduled: react.md fix(web): drop the previous account's vote
reason: Pending state was a single value, so switching accounts mid-request cleared the earlier account's in-flight vote and allowed a second overlapping vote.

expected.claim: pendingKey holds one key for the whole hook. If the viewer switches accounts and votes again before the first request settles, setPendingKey overwrites the earlier account's pending marker, so that account looks idle and can submit a second vote while the first is still in flight. Track pending per account/key.

title: Automation fix: flaky serializes concurrent identical stable-batch persistence (merge queue #2931)
reason: Advisory lock hashed the raw batch id string, so different UUID spellings (case) took different locks and could race the unique indexes.

expected.claim: The advisory lock key is built from the batch id text as supplied. UUIDs that differ only in case map to different hashes and so different locks, but the same row; concurrent inserts can both pass the lock and collide on the unique index. Canonicalize the UUID before hashing, e.g. cast to uuid.

title: perf(topics): unlink topic aliases through bounded, resumable deletion
reason: The partial index on unlink_topic_id did not cover the id ordering used when paging pending unlinks, so the paged query still sorted; index was extended to (unlink_topic_id, id).

expected.claim: The new bounded unlink flow pages pending aliases by unlink_topic_id ordered by id, but this partial index only covers unlink_topic_id. Include id in the index so the paged query is index-ordered rather than sorting each page.

title: Automation scheduled: translation-safety.md fix(web): require a content language on MarkdownContent
reason: Producer added a nullable author_aside.lingua_rs_detected_language field to the post-detail contract; the native .NET client DTO did not preserve it, failing the fixture round-trip gate on client PRs.

expected.claim: This adds a new field to the post-detail author_aside response. The native clients round-trip the published fixture strictly, so the contract change needs a coordinated client DTO update (or a note in the PR) or client CI breaks.

title: feat(households): add household MCP REST twins
reason: Producer published a new GET /api/v1/me/individual contract and fixture; native Swift/.NET clients had no typed support, so their registry and endpoint coverage gates failed until a client PR landed.

expected.claim: This publishes a new endpoint and canonical fixture consumed by the strict native contract gates. The native Swift and .NET clients need matching typed models and registry entries, so landing this alone will fail their coverage checks; coordinate or stage the client change.

title: chore(deps): standardize Dependabot policy
reason: Generic minor-and-patch and security buckets grouped unrelated dependencies together instead of the repo package-family grouping; replaced with evidence-backed family groups.

expected.claim: Grouping all npm (and likewise Actions, NuGet, Swift) minor/patch and security updates into catch-all buckets couples unrelated upgrades in a single PR. The repo dependency policy groups by package family, so define family groups and leave singletons ungrouped.

title: fix(dependabot): accept Buffer raw diffs in Swift Android repair
reason: Repair parser required mode 100644 for every file, but the allowed Skip materializer script is 100755, so any Skip PR including it failed closed.

expected.claim: The raw-diff parser demands both modes be 100644 for all paths, but the executable materializer script that the classifier explicitly allows is tracked as 100755. A PR touching it will always be rejected, so allow the executable mode for that single path and test it.
